words.ex_cn: 他在股票市场上交易期货。
words.en: Futures are financial contracts obligating the buyer to purchase an asset or the seller to sell an asset at a predetermined future date and price.

words.tr: n. 差距；隔阂；缺口；缝隙；
words.ex: There is a big gap between rich and poor.
words.ex_cn: 富人和穷人之间有很大的差距。
words.en: A gap is a space between two things or a hole in the middle of something solid.

words.tr: n. 齿轮装置； v. “gear”的现在分词；
words.ex: The bike's gearing helps it climb hills easily.
words.ex_cn: 这辆自行车的齿轮装置让它更容易爬坡。
words.en: Gearing refers to the ratio of a company's debt to its equity capital, often used as a measure of financial risk. It can also refer to the arrangement of gears in a machine.

words.ex: The ad used a cheap gimmick to attract customers.
words.ex_cn: 这个广告用了一个廉价的噱头来吸引顾客。
words.en: A gimmick is a trick or device intended to attract attention, publicity, or trade.

words.tr: n. 目标；进球得分；球门；
words.ex: His goal is to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的目标是按时完成项目。
words.en: A goal is an aim or purpose that a person or a group of people is trying to achieve.

words.tr: v. 离开；进行；“go”的现在分词； adj. 现有的； n. 离去；进展；
words.ex: He is going home after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后要离开回家。
words.en: The act of moving or proceeding; the condition of roads or weather for traveling; the act of leaving a place.

words.ex: The going rate for a hotel room in this area is $150 per night.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区酒店房间的通行价格是每晚150美元。
words.en: The going rate is the usual or current amount of money that is charged or paid for something.

words.ex: The store sells many kinds of goods.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售各种商品。
words.en: Goods are items that are made to be sold.

words.ex: He showed goodwill by helping his neighbor for free.
words.ex_cn: 他通过免费帮助邻居表现出善意。
words.en: A friendly or cooperative attitude or feeling towards others, especially in a business context.

words.ex: The company will go public next year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司明年将上市。
words.en: To offer shares of a private corporation to the public in a new stock issuance. Public share issuance allows a company to raise capital from public investors.

words.tr: phrase. 努力应对，与……作斗争，设法解决（难题或困境）
words.ex: He grapples with difficult questions every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都在努力应对难题。
words.en: If you grapple with a problem or difficulty, you try hard to solve it.

words.ex: He filed a grievance about the unfair treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他因不公平的对待提出了不满。
words.en: A grievance is a feeling of resentment over something believed to be wrong or unfair.

words.ex: The gross income of the company is $5 million.
words.ex_cn: 公司的总收入是500万美元。
words.en: If you describe something as gross, you mean it is very obvious, unacceptable, or unpleasant.

words.ex: The company's gross margin has improved significantly this quarter.
words.ex_cn: n. 公司本季度的毛利率显著提高。
words.en: Gross margin is the difference between revenue and cost of goods sold, divided by revenue. It is often expressed as a percentage.

words.ex: The company reported a significant increase in gross profit this quarter.
words.ex_cn: 该公司本季度报告了毛利的显著增长。
words.en: Gross profit is the profit a company makes after deducting the costs associated with making and selling its products, or the costs associated with providing its services.

words.ex: The gross yield of the investment was higher than expected.
words.ex_cn: 这项投资的总收益率比预期的要高。
words.en: The total return on an investment before any deductions.

words.ex: He gradually learned to ride a bike.
words.ex_cn: 他渐渐学会了骑自行车。
words.en: If something changes or is done gradually, it changes or is done in small stages over a long period of time, rather than suddenly.

words.tr:
n. 组；群；集团；
v. （使）形成组；
words.ex: The students are in a group of five.
words.ex_cn: 这些学生组成一个五人小组。
words.en: A group is a number of people or things that are located, gathered, or classed together.

words.tr: v. 生长；成长；渐渐变成；种植；
words.ex: The plant grows quickly in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这株植物在春天长得很快。
words.en: If someone or something grows, they increase in size, amount, or degree, often over a period of time.

words.ex: The growth of the plant is slow in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这植物在冬天生长缓慢。
words.en: The process of increasing in physical size, number, value, or strength.

words.tr:
v. 保证；确保；
n. 保证；保证书；
words.ex: The store guarantees a refund if you are not happy.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不满意，商店保证退款。
words.en: A guarantee is a formal promise that certain conditions will be fulfilled, especially that a product will be repaired or replaced if it is not of a specified quality.

words.ex: Follow the guidelines to pass the test.
words.ex_cn: 遵循指南以通过考试。
words.en: Guidelines are general rules, principles, or pieces of advice that help you to do something or to decide what to do in a particular situation.

words.ex: He will hand in his homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天交作业。
words.en: To give something to someone in authority, especially a piece of work or a document.

words.tr: phrase. v. 提交辞呈；正式通知辞职
words.ex: He decided to hand in his notice at work.
words.ex_cn: 他决定向公司递交辞职信。
words.en: To formally inform one's employer that one will be leaving their job.

words.tr:
v. 处理；操纵；
n. 把手；柄；
words.ex: He can handle difficult problems easily.
words.ex_cn: 他能轻松处理难题。
words.en: To deal with or control a situation or problem.

words.tr: phrase. 实践的；亲自动手的
words.ex: The students like hands-on activities in science class.
words.ex_cn: 学生们喜欢科学课上的实践性活动。
words.en: Involving or offering active participation rather than theory or observation.

words.ex: The car salesman used a hard sell approach to close the deal.
words.ex_cn: 汽车销售员采用了强力推销的方法来达成交易。
words.en: A hard sell is a method of selling in which the seller is very forceful and persistent in trying to persuade someone to buy something.

words.ex: The broken glass is a hazard.
words.ex_cn: 碎玻璃是危险。
words.en: A hazard is something which could be dangerous to you, your health or safety, or your plans or reputation.

words.tr:
n. 头；脑袋；上端；首脑；
v. 朝…行进；居首位；领导；
adj. 头的；主要的；
words.ex: He hurt his head when he fell.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒时伤到了头。
words.en: The upper part of the human body, or the front or upper part of the body of an animal, typically separated from the rest of the body by a neck, and containing the brain, mouth, and sense organs.

words.ex: The company follows health and safety rules.
words.ex_cn: 公司遵守健康与安全规定。
words.en: Principles and procedures designed to protect the safety and well-being of people in a workplace or environment.

words.tr:
n. 树篱；防范措施
v. 用树篱围住；限制；避免
words.ex: He planted a hedge around his garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在花园周围种了一排树篱。
words.en: A hedge is a row of bushes or small trees which have been planted along the edge of a garden, field, or road to separate it from another area or to protect it. As a verb, to hedge means to avoid committing oneself or to limit or qualify something by conditions or exceptions.

words.tr: adj. 隐藏的； v. 隐藏；“hide”的过去分词；
words.ex: The keys are hidden under the mat.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙藏在垫子下面。
words.en: If something is hidden, it is not easily noticed or found.

words.tr: n. 层次体系；等级制度；
words.ex: The company has a clear hierarchy from manager to worker.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司有一个从经理到员工的明确层次体系。
words.en: A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged according to their importance.

words.ex: The company will hire a new manager next week.
words.ex_cn: 公司下周将雇用一位新经理。
words.en: If you hire someone, you employ them or pay them to do a particular job for you.

words.ex: He bought the car on hire purchase, paying a small deposit and then monthly installments.
words.ex_cn: 他通过分期付款购买了这辆车，支付了一小笔定金，然后按月分期付款。
words.en: A system by which one pays for a thing in regular installments while having the use of it.

words.tr:
v. 打；击；碰撞；袭击；抨击；达到；
n. 打；击；碰撞；袭击；(演出等)成功；
words.ex: He hit the ball with a bat.
words.ex_cn: 他用球棒打了球。
words.en: If you hit someone or something, you deliberately touch them with a lot of force, with your hand or an object held in your hand.

words.tr: n. 持有者；拥有者；支架
words.ex: The holder of the ticket won a prize.
words.ex_cn: 票的持有者中了奖。
words.en: A holder is a person or thing that holds something.

words.tr: phrase. 控股公司；持有其他公司股份的公司
words.ex: The holding company acquired several smaller firms to expand its market share.
words.ex_cn: 这家控股公司收购了几家较小的公司以扩大其市场份额。
words.en: A holding company is a company that owns other companies' outstanding stock. It usually does not produce goods or services itself; rather, its purpose is to own shares of other companies to form a corporate group.

words.ex: The hostile neighbor shouted at us every morning.
words.ex_cn: 那个敌意的邻居每天早上都对我们大喊大叫。
words.en: If you are hostile to another person or an idea, you disagree with them or disapprove of them, often showing this in your behavior.

words.tr:
abbr. 人力资源开发；“human resources development”的缩写
abbr. 高纤维素饮食；“High Roughage Diet”的缩写
words.ex: The company invested in hrd to improve employee skills.
words.ex_cn: 公司投资于人力资源开发以提升员工技能。
words.en: An abbreviation for 'hard', often used in informal contexts to describe something difficult or challenging.

words.tr: phrase. 人力资源；人事部门
words.ex: The company hires new workers through human resources.
words.ex_cn: 公司通过人力资源部门招聘新员工。
words.en: Human resources is the department of a company that deals with the hiring, administration, and training of staff.

words.tr: n. 天花乱坠的广告宣传；炒作；
words.ex: The new phone got a lot of hype before its release.
words.ex_cn: 这款新手机在发布前受到了大量天花乱坠的广告宣传。
words.en: If someone or something is hyped, they are praised or advertised a lot in newspapers, on television, etc., especially in a way that is intended to make them seem very exciting or important.

words.tr:
n. 影响力；冲击（力）；
v. 对…产生影响；
words.ex: The new law had a big impact on education.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律对教育产生了重大影响。
words.en: The effect or influence of one person, thing, or action, on another.

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.tr: n. 含意；可能的影响（或后果）；暗示；
words.ex: The implication of his words was that he was sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他话中的含意是他很抱歉。
words.en: An implication is a possible future effect or result of an action or decision, often one that is not immediately obvious.

words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

words.ex: His income is enough to pay for rent and food.
words.ex_cn: 他的收入足以支付房租和食物。
words.en: Income is the money that a person or a company earns regularly, for example from investment or work.

words.tr: phrase. 己获收益；劳动收入
words.ex: He relied on earned income to support his family.
words.ex_cn: 他依靠劳动收入来养家。
words.en: Income derived from active participation in a trade or business, including wages, salary, tips, commissions, and bonuses.

words.tr: phrase. 非劳动所得；非工薪收入
words.ex: He relies heavily on unearned income from his family's investments.
words.ex_cn: 他主要依赖于家族投资带来的不劳而获的收入。
words.en: Income received from investments or other sources not related to employment.

words.ex: The temperature increases by one increment every hour.
words.ex_cn: 温度每小时增加一个单位。
words.en: An increment is an amount by which something increases or is increased.

words.ex: He incurred a fine for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 他因超速而招致了一笔罚款。
words.en: If you incur something unpleasant, it happens to you because of something you have done.

words.ex: The company paid indemnity for the damaged car.
words.ex_cn: 公司为损坏的汽车支付了保险赔偿。
words.en: If something provides indemnity, it provides insurance or protection against damage or loss, especially in the form of a legal agreement.

words.ex: The index of 2 in 2^3 is 3.
words.ex_cn: 2^3 中 2 的指数是 3。
words.en: An index is a system by which changes in the value of something and the rate at which it changes can be recorded, measured, or interpreted.

words.tr: phrase. 零售价格指数（衡量一篮子消费品与服务价格随时间变化的指标）
words.ex: The retail price index rose by 2% last month.
words.ex_cn: n. 上个月零售价格指数上涨了2%。
words.en: The retail price index (RPI) is a measure of inflation that tracks the changes in the cost of a basket of retail goods and services over time.

words.ex: The company's indirect costs include utilities and administrative expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司的间接成本包括公用事业费用和行政开支。
words.en: Indirect costs are expenses that are not directly accountable to a cost object (such as a particular project, facility, function or product).

words.ex: The induction of the new mayor will be held next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 新市长的就职典礼将在下周一举行。
words.en: Induction is the process or action of inducting someone to a position or organization, or the process of reasoning from specific cases to general rules.

words.ex: The city has many industrial factories.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市有许多工业工厂。
words.en: Industrial means relating to or characterized by industry.

words.ex: Workers took industrial action to protest against low wages.
words.ex_cn: 工人们采取了工作行动，抗议低工资。
words.en: Industrial action refers to any action taken by employees in the form of a strike, work-to-rule, or other forms of protest, aimed at achieving changes in their working conditions or pay.

words.ex: The study of industrial relations is crucial for understanding labor disputes.
words.ex_cn: 研究工业关系对于理解劳资纠纷至关重要。
words.en: The relationship between employers and employees, especially in industries, including the negotiation of wages, working conditions, and other aspects of employment.

words.ex: The old machine causes inefficiency in production.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧机器导致生产效率低下。
words.en: The lack of ability to do something or produce something without wasting materials, time, or energy.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；使充气；夸口；吹嘘
words.ex: He tries to inflate the balloon with his mouth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用嘴把气球吹大。
words.en: To inflate something means to cause it to increase in size by filling it with air or gas. It can also refer to increasing the amount of money in circulation, leading to a decrease in its value.

words.ex: The price of bread went up because of inflation.
words.ex_cn: 由于通货膨胀，面包的价格上涨了。
words.en: Inflation is a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.

words.ex: He infringes the rules by arriving late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到而违反了规则。
words.en: To infringe means to violate or break a law, agreement, or right.

words.tr:
adj. 最初的；开始的；
n. 首字母；
words.ex: This is the initial plan for the project.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个项目的最初计划。
words.en: The first letter of a name or word, used to represent the whole name or word.

words.ex: The company wants to innovate its production process.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司想改革它的生产流程。
words.en: To innovate means to introduce changes and new ideas in the way something is done or made.

words.tr:
n. 输入；
v. 输入；
words.ex: The computer needs user input to work.
words.ex_cn: 计算机需要用户输入才能工作。
words.en: Input is information that is put into a system or machine so that it can operate.

words.tr:
adj. 无力偿付债务的；破产的
n. 破产者；无力偿还者
words.ex: The company went insolvent after years of financial mismanagement.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司在多年的财务管理不善后破产了。
words.en: If a person or organization is insolvent, they do not have enough money to pay their debts.

words.ex: He paid the first installment last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周支付了第一期分期付款。
words.en: An installment is one of the amounts, usually equal, into which a debt is divided for payment at stated intervals over a fixed period.

words.ex: He insured his car against accidents.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的车投保了意外险。
words.en: If you insure yourself or your property, you pay money to an insurance company so that if you become ill or if your property is damaged or stolen, the company will pay you a sum of money.

words.ex: He bought insurance for his car.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的车买了保险。
words.en: Insurance is an arrangement in which you pay money to a company, and they pay money to you if something unpleasant happens to you, for example if your property is stolen or damaged, or if you get a serious illness.

words.tr:
n. 兴趣；利息；利益；
v. 使产生兴趣；
words.ex: He has a strong interest in painting.
words.ex_cn: 他对绘画有浓厚的兴趣。
words.en: If you have an interest in something, you want to learn or hear more about it.

words.ex: The bank raised the interest rate last month.
words.ex_cn: 银行上个月提高了利率。
words.en: The interest rate is the percentage of an amount of money which is paid for its use for a specified time, usually expressed as an annual percentage rate.

words.tr: adj. 暂时的；临时的；期间的；
words.ex: He is the interim manager until a new one is hired.
words.ex_cn: 在招聘到新的经理之前，他是临时经理。
words.en: An interim is a period of time between one event, process, or period and another, especially one of temporary nature.

words.ex: The factory adopted intermittent production to save energy.
words.ex_cn: 工厂采用间歇生产以节省能源。
words.en: Production that occurs at irregular intervals rather than continuously.

words.tr:
n. 面试；访谈；
v. 面试；接见；
words.ex: He has an interview tomorrow for a new job.
words.ex_cn: 他明天有一场新工作的面试。
words.en: An interview is a formal meeting at which someone is asked questions in order to find out if they are suitable for a job or a course of study.

words.tr: n. 被面试者；被采访者；
words.ex: The interviewee answered all the questions calmly.
words.ex_cn: 被面试者冷静地回答了所有问题。
words.en: A person who is interviewed.

words.ex: The interviewer asked him about his work experience.
words.ex_cn: 采访者问他关于他的工作经验。
words.en: An interviewer is a person who asks someone questions at an interview.

words.ex: He will introduce his friend to the class.
words.ex_cn: 他将向全班介绍他的朋友。
words.en: If you introduce someone, you tell someone else their name so that they can know each other.

words.ex: The store made an inventory of all the products.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有商品做了一份清单。
words.en: An inventory is a detailed list of all the items in a place.

words.ex: The company maintains a buffer inventory to mitigate supply chain disruptions.
words.ex_cn: 公司保持缓冲库存以缓解供应链中断。
words.en: A buffer inventory refers to a supply of goods held in reserve to protect against unforeseen shortages or delays in the supply chain.

words.ex: The company is managing its capacity inventory to meet fluctuating demand.
words.ex_cn: 公司正在管理其产能库存以应对需求波动。
words.en: A record of the maximum output a system, facility, or resource can produce under normal operating conditions.

words.ex: The company implemented a cycle inventory system to optimize stock levels.
words.ex_cn: 公司实施了周期库存系统以优化库存水平。
words.en: The inventory held to meet expected demand between replenishment cycles, balancing ordering costs and holding costs.

words.ex: The company maintains a decoupling inventory to handle unexpected delays in the supply chain.
words.ex_cn: 公司保持缓冲库存以应对供应链中的意外延迟。
words.en: Decoupling inventory refers to the stock held to ensure that production can continue smoothly even if there are disruptions in the supply chain.

words.ex: The company has a large finished goods inventory at the end of the quarter.
words.ex_cn: 公司在季度末拥有大量的成品库存。
words.en: The stock of completed products that are ready to be sold or distributed.

words.tr: phrase. 管道库存，指在生产或供应链中正在运输或加工过程中的库存。
words.ex: The company needs to reduce its pipeline inventory to improve cash flow.
words.ex_cn: 该公司需要减少其管道库存以改善现金流。
words.en: Inventory that is in the process of being transported or manufactured within a supply chain.

words.ex: The company keeps a detailed record of its raw materials inventory.
words.ex_cn: 公司对其原材料库存保持详细记录。
words.en: The stock of materials that a company holds for use in the production process.

words.ex: The factory keeps work-in-progress inventory for unfinished cars.
words.ex_cn: 工厂为未完成的汽车保留在制品库存。
words.en: Goods that are in the process of being manufactured but are not yet completed.

words.ex: He invests money in stocks.
words.ex_cn: 他投资股票。
words.en: If you invest in something, or if you invest a sum of money, you use your money in a way that you hope will increase its value, for example by putting it in a bank, or buying shares or property.

words.ex: He made an investment in a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他投资了一家小企业。
words.en: An investment is an amount of money that you invest in something.

words.ex: The investor gave money to the new business.
words.ex_cn: 这位投资者为这家新企业提供了资金。
words.en: An investor is a person or organization that puts money into financial schemes, property, etc. with the expectation of achieving a profit.

words.tr:
n. 发票；发货单；
v. 开发票；记清单；
words.ex: He paid the bill after receiving the invoice.
words.ex_cn: 他收到发票后付了款。
words.en: An invoice is a document that lists goods or services that have been provided and says how much money you owe for them.

words.tr: adj. 无法改变的；不能取消的
words.ex: The decision was irrevocable.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定是不可撤销的。
words.en: If a decision, action, or process is irrevocable, it cannot be changed or reversed.

words.tr:
n. 问题；重要议题；发行（物）；
v. 发行；
words.ex: The main issue is lack of money.
words.ex_cn: 主要问题是缺乏资金。
words.en: An issue is an important subject or problem that people are talking about or arguing about.

words.ex: The company announced a rights issue to raise money.
words.ex_cn: 公司宣布了配股以筹集资金。
words.en: A rights issue is an offering of common stock to existing shareholders, giving them the right to purchase additional shares at a discount to the current market price.

words.ex: He works in information technology at a big company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家大公司从事信息技术工作。
words.en: Information technology refers to the use of computers, storage, networking and other physical devices, infrastructure and processes to create, process, store, secure and exchange all forms of electronic data.

words.tr: n. 一件物品或商品；项目；一则；
words.ex: This item is on sale for $5.
words.ex_cn: 这件商品正在促销，售价5美元。
words.en: An item is one of a collection or list of objects.

words.ex: He got a new job last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周找到了一份新工作。
words.en: A job is the work that someone does regularly in order to earn money.

words.tr: phrase. 职位描述；工作描述；职责说明
words.ex: He read the job description before the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在面试前读了职位描述。
words.en: A job description is a written account of all the duties and responsibilities involved in a particular job or position.

words.tr: phrase. 一批卖出的杂货；（整批的）杂货
words.ex: The store sold a job lot of assorted items at a discount.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店以折扣价出售了一批各种物品的混合批发。
words.en: A job lot is a quantity of goods, often of mixed or miscellaneous items, sold or bought together at a lower price than if sold separately.

words.tr: phrase. 就业流动性；工作变动
words.ex: Job mobility has increased significantly with the advent of remote work.
words.ex_cn: 随着远程工作的出现，职业流动性显著增加。
words.en: The ability of an individual to change jobs within the same company or move to a different company, often to improve their career prospects or salary.

words.ex: The company implemented job rotation to keep employees engaged and prevent monotony.
words.ex_cn: 公司实施了工作轮岗，以保持员工的参与度并防止单调乏味。
words.en: Job rotation is a management strategy where employees are moved between two or more jobs in a planned manner to expose them to different functions and roles within an organization.

words.ex: He has high job satisfaction because he likes his work.
words.ex_cn: 他工作满意度很高，因为他喜欢自己的工作。
words.en: Job satisfaction refers to the level of contentment employees feel with their job, which can be influenced by various factors such as work environment, salary, and opportunities for advancement.

words.ex: The job shop specializes in producing custom parts for various industries.
words.ex_cn: 这家加工厂专门为各个行业生产定制零件。
words.en: A job shop is a type of manufacturing process in which small batches of a variety of custom products are made. It is characterized by its flexibility and the ability to produce a wide range of products in low volumes.

words.ex: He is jobbing as a painter during the summer.
words.ex_cn: 他夏天做临时油漆工。
words.en: The act of doing casual or occasional work.

words.tr:
adj. 联合的；共同的；
n. 关节；接合处；
words.ex: They signed a joint agreement to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一项联合协议来保护环境。
words.en: A joint is a place where two things are joined together, especially the place where two bones are connected in a person's or animal's body.

words.ex: They decided to open a joint bank account to manage their shared expenses.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定开设一个联名银行账户来管理共同的开支。
words.en: A joint bank account is a bank account shared by two or more individuals. Any account holder can deposit or withdraw funds and sign checks without the consent of the other account holders.

words.ex: He reads a science journal every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周读一本科学期刊。
words.en: A journal is a newspaper or magazine that deals with a particular subject or professional activity.

words.tr: n. 管辖权；司法权；裁判权；
words.ex: The court has jurisdiction over this case.
words.ex_cn: 法院对这个案件有管辖权。
words.en: The official power to make legal decisions and judgments.

words.ex: Investing in junk bonds can be very risky.
words.ex_cn: 投资垃圾债券可能非常冒险。
words.en: Junk bonds are high-yield bonds that carry a higher risk of default than investment-grade bonds.

words.ex: I receive a lot of junk mail every day.
words.ex_cn: 我每天收到很多邮寄宣传品。
words.en: Unsolicited mail, typically of a commercial nature, sent in large quantities.

words.tr:
adj. 恰好够用的；适时制的；零库存的
n. 适时制；零库存
words.ex: The factory uses just-in-time delivery to save space.
words.ex_cn: 工厂使用准时制交付来节省空间。
words.en: Just-in-time refers to a production strategy that strives to improve a business's return on investment by reducing in-process inventory and associated carrying costs.

words.tr:
adj. 关键的；
n. 钥匙；关键；
words.ex: This is a key step to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这是解决问题的关键步骤。
words.en: A key is a specially shaped piece of metal that you place in a lock and turn in order to open or lock a door, or to start or stop the engine of a vehicle.

words.tr: adj. 最低的；可拆卸的；不可抵抗的；压倒一切的; n. 打倒的一击；混战；降低
words.ex: They offered a knock-down price for the old car.
words.ex_cn: 他们对这辆旧车给出了最低价格。
words.en: If something is knock-down, it is designed to be easily assembled and disassembled, or it is extremely low in price or overwhelming in effect.

words.tr: n. 实际知识；技术；窍门
words.ex: He has the know-how to fix the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他有修理这台机器的诀窍。
words.en: Practical knowledge or expertise in a particular field or area.

words.tr:
n. 标签；
v. 用标签标明；
words.ex: The bottle has a label with the name of the drink.
words.ex_cn: 瓶子上有一个写着饮料名称的标签。
words.en: A label is a piece of paper, polymer, cloth, metal, or other material affixed to a container or article, on which is written or printed information or symbols about the product or item.

words.tr: n. 劳动；体力劳动；劳工；
words.ex: Hard labor helps build strong character.
words.ex_cn: 辛勤的劳动有助于培养坚强的品格。
words.en: Work, especially physical work; to work hard.

words.ex: Many people look for jobs in the labor market.
words.ex_cn: 许多人在劳动力市场找工作。
words.en: The labor market refers to the supply of and demand for labor, in which employees provide the supply and employers provide the demand.

words.ex: The company is known for its excellent labor relations.
words.ex_cn: 该公司以其良好的劳资关系而闻名。
words.en: Labor relations refer to the relationship between employers and employees, particularly in terms of working conditions, wages, and collective bargaining.

words.tr: phrase. 劳动力短缺：指某个行业或地区缺乏足够的劳动力资源，导致无法满足生产或服务的需求。
words.ex: The factory has a labor shortage and needs more workers.
words.ex_cn: 工厂劳动力短缺，需要更多工人。
words.en: A situation where there are not enough workers to fill the available jobs.

words.tr:
v. 发射；发起；启动；
n. 发射；投掷；启动；
words.ex: They will launch a rocket tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将发射一枚火箭。
words.en: To launch something means to send it into the air, space, or water, especially with a lot of force or effort, or to start an activity, event, or project.

words.ex: The layout of the room makes it feel bigger.
words.ex_cn: 房间的布局让它显得更大。
words.en: The way in which the parts of something are arranged or laid out.

words.tr:
v. 引导；领导；带头；
n. 主导地位；铅；领先；
words.ex: The teacher leads the students to the library.
words.ex_cn: 老师带领学生去图书馆。
words.en: To be in charge of a group, country, or situation; to guide or direct in a course; a position of advantage in a contest or competition; a heavy, malleable, ductile, bluish-white, dense metallic element.

words.tr: phrase. 前置时间；从订货到交货的周期；生产准备期
words.ex: The project was delayed due to long lead times in acquiring materials.
words.ex_cn: 由于获取材料的前导时间过长，项目被推迟了。
words.en: The period of time between the initiation and completion of a production process.

words.ex: He handed out a leaflet about the event.
words.ex_cn: 他分发了一份关于该活动的传单。
words.en: A leaflet is a small sheet of printed paper that gives you information or advertises something.

words.tr:
n. 租契；
v. 出租；
words.ex: He signed a lease for the apartment.
words.ex_cn: 他签了公寓的租契。
words.en: A lease is a legal agreement by which the owner of a building, a piece of land, or something such as a car allows someone else to use it for a period of time in return for money.

words.ex: He hired a legal lawyer to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他请了一位法律律师来帮助他。
words.en: Relating to the law or to lawyers, or permitted or required by law.

words.ex: Can you lend me your pen?
words.ex_cn: 你能把你的笔借给我吗？
words.en: If you lend something you own to someone else, you allow them to have it or use it for a period of time, after which they must return it to you.

words.ex: The lessee pays rent every month.
words.ex_cn: 承租人每月支付租金。
words.en: A lessee is a person who holds the lease of a property.

words.ex: He chose the lesser price.
words.ex_cn: 他选择了更少的价格。
words.en: You use lesser to indicate that something is smaller in extent, degree, or amount than another thing that has been mentioned.

words.ex: He writes all the money in the ledger.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的钱都记在账本上。
words.en: A ledger is a book or collection of accounts in which account transactions are recorded.

words.ex: The company uses a nominal ledger to track its income and expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司使用名义分类账来追踪其收入和支出。
words.en: A nominal ledger is the part of a company's accounting system where all its financial transactions are recorded in nominal accounts.

words.ex: The accountant updated the purchase ledger with the latest transactions.
words.ex_cn: 会计用最新的交易更新了采购分类账。
words.en: A purchase ledger is a record of all purchases made by a business, typically used in accounting to track expenditures and manage financial records.

words.ex: He checks the sales ledger every Friday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周五检查销售账簿。
words.en: A sales ledger is a financial document that records all sales transactions of a business, including details of the sales, the amounts, and the customers involved. It is used to track sales revenue and manage customer accounts.

words.tr:
n. 杠杆；杠杆作用；影响力
v. 举债经营；充分利用
words.ex: The mechanic used a lever to lift the car.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用杠杆来抬起汽车。
words.en: Leverage refers to the use of a lever or the mechanical advantage gained by using a lever. In finance, it refers to the use of borrowed capital to increase the potential return of an investment.

words.ex: He accepted liability for the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他承担了事故的责任。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a liability, you mean that they cause a lot of problems or embarrassment.

words.tr: n. 倾向; 责任，义务; 债务，负债
words.ex: The company's main liabilities are its bank loans and unpaid bills.
words.ex_cn: 该公司的主要负债是银行贷款和未付账单。
words.en: Liabilities refer to the financial debts or obligations that a company or individual owes to others, which must be settled over time through the transfer of economic benefits including money, goods, or services.

words.ex: He got a driver's license last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周拿到了驾照。
words.en: A license is an official document which gives you permission to do, use, or own something.

words.tr: phrase. 生活周期；存在周期
words.ex: The life cycle of a butterfly includes egg, larva, pupa, and adult.
words.ex_cn: 蝴蝶的生活周期包括卵、幼虫、蛹和成虫。
words.en: The series of changes that a living thing goes through from the beginning of its life until death.

words.ex: He is likely to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他很可能赢得比赛。
words.en: If something is likely, it will probably happen or is expected.

words.ex: The line process is crucial in the manufacturing industry.
words.ex_cn: 线过程在制造业中至关重要。
words.en: A method of production in which a product is assembled in a sequence of steps by different workers or machines.

words.tr:
n. 连接物；
v. 连接；联系；
words.ex: The chain has a broken link.
words.ex_cn: 这条链子有一个断了的连接物。
words.en: A link between two people, organizations, or places is a connection between them.

words.tr:
n. 液体；
adj. 液态的；
words.ex: Water is a common liquid.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的液体。
words.en: A liquid is a substance which is not solid but which flows and can be poured, for example water.

words.tr: v. 清算；变卖；消除；铲除
words.ex: The company will liquidate its assets to pay debts.
words.ex_cn: 公司将变卖资产来偿还债务。
words.en: To liquidate a company means to sell its assets in order to pay its debts, or to sell an asset for cash.

words.tr: n. 资产流动性；资产变现能力
words.ex: The company is facing a liquidity crisis due to the sudden drop in sales.
words.ex_cn: 由于销售额的突然下降，该公司正面临流动性危机。
words.en: Liquidity refers to the availability of liquid assets to a market or company. Liquid assets are those that can be quickly converted into cash without significantly affecting their value.

words.ex: The company went through liquidation after going bankrupt.
words.ex_cn: 该公司在破产后进行了停业清理。
words.en: The process of bringing a business to an end and distributing its assets to claimants.

words.ex: The liquidator was appointed to handle the company's assets.
words.ex_cn: 清算人被任命来处理公司的资产。
words.en: A liquidator is a person or entity appointed to wind up the affairs of a company or partnership, especially in the context of bankruptcy or dissolution.

words.tr: v. 列出；“list”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 列出的；上市的；
words.ex: The teacher listed the homework on the board.
words.ex_cn: 老师把作业写在了黑板上。
words.en: Included in a list, especially of companies whose shares are traded on a stock exchange.

words.tr: n. 清单；名单；上市； v. 列出；“list”的现在分词；
words.ex: He checked the listing before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前检查了清单。
words.en: A listing is a list or a catalog of items, especially one that is published or made available in a particular form.

words.ex: He loves reading English literature.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢阅读英语文学。
words.en: Literature consists of written works, especially those considered to have artistic or intellectual value.

words.ex: They will litigate the contract dispute next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将就合同纠纷提起诉讼。
words.en: To litigate means to engage in a legal proceeding or lawsuit, either as a plaintiff or defendant, to resolve a dispute.

words.ex: The bank gave a loan to the student.
words.ex_cn: 银行向学生提供了一笔贷款。
words.en: A loan is a sum of money that you borrow.

words.ex: The company has a simple logo on its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的产品上有一个简单的标志。
words.en: A logo is a design or symbol used by a company to identify its products, services, or itself.

words.ex: He lost his keys yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天丢了钥匙。
words.en: If you lose something, you no longer have it or you cannot find it.

words.ex: He didn't give up, even though some called him a loser.
words.ex_cn: 他没有放弃，即使有些人称他为失败者。
words.en: A loser is someone who is not successful in a particular situation or who does not achieve what they set out to do.

words.ex: The company suffered a big loss last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司去年遭受了巨大损失。
words.en: Loss is the fact of no longer having something or having less of it than you used to have, or the process by which this happens.

words.ex: There are a lot of books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书架上有许多书。
words.en: A lot refers to a large number or amount of something. It can also mean a piece of land or someone's fate or destiny.

words.ex: His loyalty to his friends never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的忠诚从未改变。
words.en: The quality of being loyal to someone or something.

words.ex: He reads a magazine every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上读一本杂志。
words.en: A magazine is a type of thin book with large pages and a paper cover which contains articles, photographs, and advertisements, usually on a particular subject or aimed at a particular readership.

words.tr: phrase. 通过邮政发出的类似广告的宣传材料；邮寄广告；邮购目录
words.ex: The company conducted a mail shot to promote their new product.
words.ex_cn: 公司通过邮寄广告来推广他们的新产品。
words.en: A mail shot is a large number of advertising documents sent by post to a large number of addresses at the same time.

words.tr:
n. 辩论；讨论；
v. 辩论；讨论；
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: If you maintain something, you continue to have it, and do not let it stop or grow weaker.

words.ex: The cost of maintenance is low for this car.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的维持费用很低。
words.en: The process of preserving a condition or situation or the state of being preserved.

words.tr:
adj. 主要的；
n. 大调；主修课；
words.ex: Math is a major subject in school.
words.ex_cn: 数学是学校里的主要科目。
words.en: A major is a student's principal field of study or specialization in college or university.

words.tr: phrase. 主要股权；绝对控股
words.ex: The company was acquired through a majority shareholding.
words.ex_cn: 该公司通过绝对控股被收购。
words.en: A majority shareholding is ownership of more than 50% of a company's shares by an individual or another company.

words.ex: The rain made the road wet.
words.ex_cn: 雨使得道路变湿了。
words.en: To create, produce, or prepare something, especially by putting parts together or by combining materials.

words.ex: The company specializes in make-to-order furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司专门从事按订单生产的家具。
words.en: Made according to the specifications of an individual customer.

words.ex: The company uses a make-to-stock strategy to ensure products are always available.
words.ex_cn: 该公司采用按库存生产策略，以确保产品始终有货。
words.en: A production strategy where products are manufactured based on forecasted demand and stored in inventory until they are sold.

words.ex: Good management helps a company grow.
words.ex_cn: 良好的管理有助于公司发展。
words.en: The control and organization of something, especially a business and its employees.

words.tr: phrase. 中层管理人员；中层管理
words.ex: Middle management often finds itself caught between the demands of upper management and the needs of the employees.
words.ex_cn: 中层管理人员常常发现自己夹在上层管理的要求和员工的需求之间。
words.en: Middle management refers to the level of management in an organization that is below top management and above the lowest level of management. It is responsible for the implementation of the strategies and policies set by top management.

words.ex: The senior management made the final decision.
words.ex_cn: 高级管理层做出了最终决定。
words.en: Senior management refers to the individuals at the highest level of organizational hierarchy who have the day-to-day responsibilities of managing a company or corporation.

words.ex: He has a managerial role in the company.
words.ex_cn: 他在公司中担任管理职务。
words.en: relating to the job of a manager

words.ex: The manager approved the new project.
words.ex_cn: 经理批准了新项目。
words.en: A manager is a person who is responsible for running part of or the whole of a business organization.

words.ex: The plant manager checks the machines every morning.
words.ex_cn: 工厂经理每天早上检查机器。
words.en: A plant manager is responsible for the overall operation of a manufacturing plant, including production, maintenance, quality control, and safety.

words.tr: phrase. 部门经理；业务经理
words.ex: The line manager checks the workers' progress every day.
words.ex_cn: 直线经理每天检查工人的进展。
words.en: A line manager is a manager to whom a worker directly reports and who is responsible for their day-to-day management.

words.tr: phrase. 员工经理；负责管理员工的主管
words.ex: The staff manager helps workers with their problems.
words.ex_cn: 员工经理帮助员工解决他们的问题。
words.en: A staff manager is a person responsible for managing the staff within an organization, including hiring, training, and overseeing employees.

words.tr: phrase. 管理账户；管理会计
words.ex: The management accounts provide detailed financial information to the company's executives.
words.ex_cn: 管理账户为公司高管提供详细的财务信息。
words.en: Management accounts are financial reports prepared for the internal use of a company's management to assist in decision-making and control.

words.ex: Matrix management allows employees to report to more than one manager.
words.ex_cn: 矩阵管理允许员工向多个经理汇报。
words.en: A system of management in which individuals report to more than one supervisor or leader, typically combining functional and project management.

words.ex: He works in a company that uses a management information system.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家使用管理信息系统公司工作。
words.en: A management information system (MIS) is an organized system that gathers, stores, and disseminates information in the form of reports and other outputs to support decision-making in an organization.

words.tr:
n. 人员配备
v. 操作；工作；“man”的现在分词
words.ex: The company is facing challenges in manning its new production line.
words.ex_cn: 公司在新生产线的人员配备上面临挑战。
words.en: To man something means to provide it with the people needed to operate it or to do the work involved.

words.ex: The project needs more manpower to finish on time.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目需要更多人力才能按时完成。
words.en: Manpower refers to the total number of people available to work or to perform a particular task.

words.ex: The company is investing heavily in training its manpower resources.
words.ex_cn: 该公司正在大力投资培训其劳动力资源。
words.en: The personnel available for work or service in a particular area or organization.

words.tr:
adj. 手工的；体力的；
n. 说明书；
words.ex: He made a manual copy of the letter.
words.ex_cn: 他手工抄写了一封信。
words.en: A manual is a book which tells you how to do something or how a piece of machinery works.

words.tr:
n. 制造；
v. （用机器大量）制造；虚构；捏造；
words.ex: The manufacture of cars needs many workers.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的制造需要很多工人。
words.en: To manufacture something means to make it in a factory, usually in large quantities.

words.ex: The manufacturer makes cars in this factory.
words.ex_cn: 这家制造商在这家工厂生产汽车。
words.en: A manufacturer is a person or company that produces goods in large quantities, especially in a factory.

words.tr: n. 制造业； v. 制造；“manufacture”的现在分词；
words.ex: Manufacturing is important for the country's economy.
words.ex_cn: 制造业对国家经济很重要。
words.en: The process of converting raw materials into finished products, especially by means of a large-scale industrial operation.

words.ex: The manufacturing industry makes cars and phones.
words.ex_cn: 制造业生产汽车和手机。
words.en: The sector of the economy concerned with the production of goods in factories.

words.tr: n. 差额；边缘；净利润；余地；
words.ex: The profit margin is five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 利润差额是五美元。
words.en: The margin is the edge or border of something, or the difference between two amounts, especially the difference between the cost of producing something and the price it is sold for.

words.ex: The company's gross margin has improved significantly this quarter.
words.ex_cn: n. 公司本季度的毛利率显著提高。
words.en: Gross margin is the difference between revenue and cost of goods sold, divided by revenue. It is often expressed as a percentage.

words.ex: The company reported a net margin of 10% for the quarter.
words.ex_cn: 该公司报告季度净利润率为10%。
words.en: Net margin is a measure of profitability calculated as net income divided by revenue. It represents the percentage of revenue that remains as profit after all expenses have been deducted.

words.tr: n. 加价；毛利；涨价幅度
words.ex: The store adds a 20% markup to the cost of goods.
words.ex_cn: 商店在商品成本上加了20%的利润。
words.en: The amount added to the cost price of goods to cover overhead and profit.

words.tr:
n. 市场；行情；商场；销路；
v. 营销；
words.ex: The market sells fresh vegetables every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这个市场每天早上卖新鲜蔬菜。
words.en: A market is a place where goods are bought and sold, or an area or country where there is a demand for particular goods or services.

words.tr: phrase. 价廉质次（的）；低端市场（的）
words.ex: The company decided to launch a down market version of their product to attract more customers.
words.ex_cn: 公司决定推出一款低档产品版本，以吸引更多顾客。
words.en: A market condition characterized by declining prices or values.

words.ex: They decided to open an up market restaurant in the city center.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定在市中心开一家高档餐厅。
words.en: Up market refers to products, services, or establishments that are aimed at high-income or affluent consumers, often characterized by higher quality, exclusivity, and premium pricing.

words.ex: The marketing mix is crucial for determining the success of a product launch.
words.ex_cn: 营销组合对于产品发布的成功至关重要。
words.en: The combination of factors that can be controlled by a company to influence consumers to purchase its products.

words.tr: phrase. 市场领导者；行业龙头；市场占有率最高的公司
words.ex: The company has established itself as the market leader in the smartphone industry.
words.ex_cn: 该公司已经在智能手机行业确立了自己作为市场领导者的地位。
words.en: A market leader is a company that has the largest market share in a particular industry and often sets the trends and standards that others follow.

words.ex: The company has found a profitable market niche in eco-friendly products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司在环保产品中找到了一个有利可图的市场细分。
words.en: A market niche is a small, specialized segment of a larger market, often with specific needs or preferences.

words.tr: phrase. 市场渗透率；市场渗透（指产品或服务在目标市场中所占份额或渗透程度）
words.ex: The company is focusing on increasing its market penetration in the Asian region.
words.ex_cn: 该公司正专注于在亚洲地区提高其市场渗透率。
words.en: Market penetration refers to the extent to which a product or service is recognized and bought by customers in a particular market.

words.ex: Market segmentation is crucial for targeting specific customer groups.
words.ex_cn: 市场分割对于定位特定的客户群体至关重要。
words.en: Market segmentation is the process of dividing a broad consumer or business market, normally consisting of existing and potential customers, into sub-groups of consumers (known as segments) based on some type of shared characteristics.

words.tr: phrase. 市场交易额；市场份额；市场占有率
words.ex: The company increased its market share by lowering prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司通过降价增加了市场交易额。
words.en: The proportion of industry sales of a particular product or service that is controlled by a company.

words.ex: The company uses mass-marketing to sell cheap toys.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司使用大众营销来销售便宜的玩具。
words.en: Mass-marketing refers to the strategy of selling products or services to a large number of customers, typically through widespread advertising campaigns.

words.ex: The master production schedule is crucial for coordinating all manufacturing activities.
words.ex_cn: 主生产计划对于协调所有制造活动至关重要。
words.en: A master production schedule (MPS) is a plan for individual commodities to be produced in each time period such as production, staffing, inventory, etc. It is usually linked to manufacturing where the plan indicates when and how much of each product will be demanded.

words.tr: phrase. 物料需求计划；一种基于计算机的信息系统，用于确定制造产品所需的原材料、零部件及组件的数量与时间安排
words.ex: The factory uses material requirements planning to order parts on time.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂使用物料需求计划来及时订购零件。
words.en: A system for calculating the materials and components needed to manufacture a product.

words.ex: Efficient materials handling can significantly reduce production costs.
words.ex_cn: 高效的物料搬运可以显著降低生产成本。
words.en: Materials handling refers to the movement, protection, storage, and control of materials and products throughout manufacturing, warehousing, distribution, consumption, and disposal.

words.tr: v. 使增加至最大限度；最大化；
words.ex: He tries to maximize his profit by selling more.
words.ex_cn: 他通过多卖东西来使利润达到最大。
words.en: To maximize something means to make it as great in amount, size, or importance as possible.

words.tr:
v. 测量；衡量；度量；
n. 衡量；量度；措施；
words.ex: He uses a ruler to measure the length of the table.
words.ex_cn: 他用尺子测量桌子的长度。
words.en: To measure something means to determine its size, amount, or degree, often by using a tool or device designed for this purpose.

words.tr:
n. 中位数；（三角形的）中线
adj. 中间值的；中间的
words.ex: The median of 3, 5, and 7 is 5.
words.ex_cn: 3、5和7的中位数是5。
words.en: The median is the middle number in a sorted, ascending or descending, list of numbers and can be more descriptive of that data set than the average.

words.ex: The mass media shows news every day.
words.ex_cn: 大众媒体每天播放新闻。
words.en: The mass media refers to the various means by which information is communicated to large numbers of people, including newspapers, magazines, television, and the internet.

words.tr: n. 销售规划；商品促销
words.ex: The store manager improved merchandising to sell more clothes.
words.ex_cn: 商店经理改进了销售规划以卖出更多衣服。
words.en: The activity of promoting the sale of goods, especially by their presentation in retail outlets.

words.ex: The two companies will merge next year.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司明年将合并。
words.en: To combine or unite to form a single entity.

words.ex: The merger of two companies created a bigger business.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司的合并创建了一家更大的企业。
words.en: A merger is the joining together of two separate companies or organizations so that they become one.

words.ex: The merit of this plan is its simplicity.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划的优点是简单。
words.en: If something has merit, it has good or worthwhile qualities.

words.ex: The company conducted a method study to improve production efficiency.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了方法研究以提高生产效率。
words.en: Method study is a systematic examination of activities to improve the use of resources and enhance efficiency.

words.ex: The middleman helped the buyer and seller agree on a price.
words.ex_cn: 中间人帮助买家和卖家达成了价格协议。
words.en: A middleman is a person who arranges business or political deals between other people.

words.ex: I prefer full milk for my morning cereal.
words.ex_cn: n. 我更喜欢在早晨的麦片中加入全脂牛奶。
words.en: Full milk refers to milk from which no fat has been removed, containing all the natural fat content.

words.ex: She prefers to drink skimmed milk instead of whole milk.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢喝脱脂牛奶而不是全脂牛奶。
words.en: Milk from which the cream has been removed.

words.tr: v. 减到最少；使最小化；
words.ex: Try to minimize waste in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 尽量减少厨房里的浪费。
words.en: To minimize something means to reduce it to the smallest possible amount or degree.

words.ex: His mission is to help poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他的使命是帮助贫困儿童。
words.en: A mission is an important task that people are given to do, especially one that involves travelling to another country.

words.ex: The new policy improves worker mobility.
words.ex_cn: 新政策提高了工人的流动性。
words.en: The ability to move or be moved freely and easily.

words.tr: adv. 适度地；不过分地；有节制地；
words.ex: He eats moderately to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他适度饮食以保持健康。
words.en: In a manner that is neither too much nor too little; to a moderate extent.

words.ex: He has a monopoly on selling ice cream in this town.
words.ex_cn: 他在这座小镇上垄断了冰淇淋的销售。
words.en: If a company, person, or state has a monopoly on something such as an industry, they have complete control over it, so that it is impossible for others to become involved in it.

words.ex: He took out a mortgage to buy his first house.
words.ex_cn: 他申请了一笔抵押贷款来购买他的第一套房子。
words.en: A mortgage is a loan of money which you get from a bank or building society in order to buy a house.

words.ex: Good teachers motivate students to learn.
words.ex_cn: 好老师激励学生学习。
words.en: To motivate someone means to provide them with a reason for doing something, especially something that requires effort.

words.tr: adj. 有动机的；有积极性的； v. 激发；“motivate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is motivated to study hard for the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他有动力努力为考试学习。
words.en: If you are motivated by something, especially a strong emotion, it causes you to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: His motivation is to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他的动机是帮助他人。
words.en: Motivation is the enthusiasm or reason for doing something.

words.ex: His motive was to help his family.
words.ex_cn: 他的动机是帮助家人。
words.en: Your motive for doing something is your reason for doing it.

words.ex: They will negotiate the price with the seller.
words.ex_cn: 他们会与卖家协商价格。
words.en: If people negotiate with each other or negotiate an agreement, they talk about a problem or a situation such as a business arrangement in order to solve the problem or complete the arrangement.

words.tr: adj. 可协商的；可转让的；可通行的
words.ex: The price is negotiable.
words.ex_cn: 价格可以商量。
words.en: If you describe something as negotiable, you mean that it can be changed or agreed upon through discussion.

words.tr:
adj. 净余的；
n. 网；
words.ex: The net profit after taxes is $500.
words.ex_cn: 缴税后的净收益是500美元。
words.en: A net is a piece of thin fabric or thread that is used to catch fish, insects, or other small animals. It can also refer to the amount of money remaining after all expenses have been deducted.

words.ex: The internet is a big network of computers.
words.ex_cn: 互联网是一个庞大的计算机网络。
words.en: A network is a system of lines or channels that cross or connect, or a group of broadcasting stations that connect for the simultaneous broadcast of a program.

words.tr: n. 商机；理想的工作或生活；
words.ex: He found a niche in selling eco-friendly phone cases.
words.ex_cn: 他在销售环保手机壳方面找到了商机。
words.en: A niche is a hollow area in a wall which has been made to hold a statue, or a comfortable or suitable position in life or employment.

words.tr:
n. 注意；通知；
v. 注意；留心；通知；
words.ex: He gave a notice about the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他发布了关于会议的通知。
words.en: If you notice something or someone, you become aware of them.

words.tr:
adj. 客观的；
n. 目标；目的；
words.ex: He gave an objective opinion about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影给出了一个客观的看法。
words.en: An objective is something that you plan to do or achieve.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；废弃的；淘汰的；
words.ex: This phone is obsolete because it doesn't work with new apps.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，因为它不能使用新应用。
words.en: Something that is obsolete is no longer needed because something better has been invented.

words.tr:
v. 提供；
n. 提供；提议；报价；
words.ex: He offers help to his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他向同学提供帮助。
words.en: If you offer something to someone, you ask them if they would like to have it or use it.

words.tr:
n. 淡季
adj. 淡季的
adv. 淡季地
words.ex: He works as a coach in the off-season.
words.ex_cn: 他在休赛期当教练。
words.en: The off-season is the time of year when a particular place or activity is less busy or popular.

words.ex: He bought an off-the-shelf computer for his work.
words.ex_cn: 他为工作买了一台现成的电脑。
words.en: Something that is off-the-shelf is available immediately and does not need to be specially made or ordered.

words.ex: He bought an off-the-peg suit for the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他为婚礼买了一套成衣西装。
words.en: Ready-made and not made to order.

words.tr: n. 开始；开口；空缺职位； v. 打开；“open”的现在分词； adj. 开始的；
words.ex: The opening of the meeting was delayed.
words.ex_cn: 会议的开始被推迟了。
words.en: An opening is a gap or hole in something, or the act of making or becoming open. It can also refer to the beginning of an event or period.

words.tr: v. 运转；操作；施行手术；
words.ex: The machine operates smoothly.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器运转顺畅。
words.en: If you operate a business or organization, you work to keep it running properly. If a business or organization operates, it carries out its work.

words.tr: phrase. 营业利润；经营利润；运营收益（扣除营业成本和营业费用后的利润）
words.ex: The company reported higher operating profits this quarter.
words.ex_cn: n. 公司本季度报告了更高的营业利润。
words.en: Operating profits refer to the profit earned from a company's core business operations, excluding non-operating income and expenses.

words.ex: The operations chart clearly outlines the steps involved in the manufacturing process.
words.ex_cn: 操作图清晰地概述了制造过程中涉及的步骤。
words.en: A diagram or chart that outlines the steps or procedures involved in a particular operation or process.

words.ex: Effective operations scheduling can significantly improve productivity.
words.ex_cn: 有效的运营调度可以显著提高生产力。
words.en: The process of arranging, controlling, and optimizing work and workloads in a production process or manufacturing process.

words.ex: He got an opportunity to work abroad.
words.ex_cn: 他得到了一个去国外工作的机会。
words.en: An opportunity is a situation in which it is possible for you to do something that you want to do.

words.ex: We optimize the route to save time.
words.ex_cn: 我们优化路线以节省时间。
words.en: To optimize something means to make it as good or as effective as possible.

words.ex: You have three options to choose from.
words.ex_cn: 你有三个选项可以选择。
words.en: An option is something that you can choose to do in preference to one or more alternatives.

words.tr: phrase. 股票期权； 股份认购权
words.ex: He received a share option as part of his job package.
words.ex_cn: 他作为工作待遇的一部分获得了股票期权。
words.en: A share option is a right given to an employee to buy shares in the company they work for at a fixed price or at a price determined by a formula.

words.ex: The organization chart clearly shows the hierarchy within the company.
words.ex_cn: 组织结构图清晰地展示了公司内部的层级关系。
words.en: A diagram that shows the structure of an organization and the relationships and relative ranks of its parts and positions/jobs.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.tr: n. 入学介绍；岗前训练；方向；取向；
words.ex: The school held an orientation for new students on Monday.
words.ex_cn: 学校在周一为新生举行了入学介绍。
words.en: The act of orienting or the state of being oriented; the determination of the relative position of something or someone (especially oneself).

words.ex: The outcome of the game was a tie.
words.ex_cn: 比赛的结果是平局。
words.en: The outcome of an activity, process, or situation is the situation that exists at the end of it.

words.ex: The outlay for the new computer was high.
words.ex_cn: 这台新电脑的花费很高。
words.en: An outlay is an amount of money that you have to spend in order to buy something or to start a project.

words.tr: n. 出口；发泄途径；经销店；折扣店
words.ex: The river flows out through an outlet.
words.ex_cn: 河水通过一个出口流出。
words.en: An outlet is a hole or pipe through which liquid or air can flow out, or a point in a wall where you can connect electrical equipment to the electricity supply.

words.ex: There is a retail outlet near the bus stop.
words.ex_cn: 公交站附近有一个零售店。
words.en: A retail outlet is a place where products are sold directly to consumers.

words.tr: n. [会计]支出；开支（outgoing 的复数形式）
words.ex: His outgoings are higher than his income.
words.ex_cn: 他的支出高于他的收入。
words.en: Expenditures or expenses, especially those incurred by a business or individual.

words.ex: He outlined the plan in one sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他用一句话概述了这个计划。
words.en: To outline means to describe something in a general way, without giving all the details, or to draw the outer edge of something.

words.ex: The factory's output increased last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂上个月的产量增加了。
words.en: The amount of something produced by a person, machine, or industry.

words.ex: The company decided to outsource its customer service.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司决定将客户服务外购。
words.en: If a company outsources work or things, it pays workers from outside the company to do the work or supply the things.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；尚未处理的；
words.ex: He is an outstanding student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名杰出的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as outstanding, you think that they are very remarkable and impressive.

words.tr:
v. 供不应求
n. 供不应求
words.ex: The new phone model over-demands the market.
words.ex_cn: 这款新手机供不应求。
words.en: A situation where the demand for something exceeds the available supply or capacity.

words.ex: He went overdrawn on his bank account.
words.ex_cn: 他的银行账户透支了。
words.en: An overdraft occurs when money is withdrawn from a bank account and the available balance goes below zero.

words.tr: phrase. 透支额度；银行允许账户持有人透支一定金额的服务
words.ex: The bank offers an overdraft facility to its customers.
words.ex_cn: 银行向客户提供透支服务。
words.en: An overdraft facility is a financial service provided by banks that allows customers to withdraw more money than they have in their account, up to a certain limit.

words.tr: v. 透支；过度往后拉；过分描述
words.ex: He overdraws his bank account every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月都透支银行账户。
words.en: To overdraw means to withdraw more money from a bank account than the account holds, resulting in a negative balance. It can also mean to exaggerate or embellish in description or representation.

words.tr: phrase. 营业间接成本；日常开支
words.ex: The overhead costs are high in this factory.
words.ex_cn: 这个工厂的间接费用很高。
words.en: Overhead costs refer to ongoing business expenses not directly attributed to creating a product or service.

words.tr: n. （企业的）一般管理费用；“overhead”的复数；
words.ex: The company reduced its overheads by cutting office supplies.
words.ex_cn: 公司通过减少办公用品来降低一般管理费用。
words.en: Overheads refer to the ongoing business expenses not directly attributed to creating a product or service. It is a key concept in understanding the financial health of a business.

words.ex: He overpaid for the old book.
words.ex_cn: 他为这本旧书付了过多的钱。
words.en: To pay more than the due amount or more than the value of something.

words.ex: He worked overtime to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他加班完成了这个项目。
words.en: Overtime refers to the time worked beyond one's regular working hours, often with additional pay.

words.ex: The report gives an overview of the project.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告对项目进行了概述。
words.en: An overview is a general summary or review of a subject.

words.ex: He owes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归功于努力工作。
words.en: If you owe money to someone, they have lent it to you and you have not yet paid it back. You can also say that you owe someone a debt of gratitude if they have helped you in a way that you feel you should thank them for.

words.ex: The job pays $30,000 p.a.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作年薪3万美元。
words.en: Per annum is a Latin phrase meaning 'for each year' and is often used in financial contexts to indicate an annual rate or amount.

words.tr: n. 包装；装箱；包装物； v. “package”的现在分词；
words.ex: The packaging of the gift was very beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 这份礼物的包装非常漂亮。
words.en: The materials in which goods are wrapped or packed, especially commercially.

words.ex: The parent company decided to merge its subsidiaries to streamline operations.
words.ex_cn: 母公司决定合并其子公司以简化运营。
words.en: A parent company is a company that owns enough voting stock in another firm to control management and operations by influencing or electing its board of directors.

words.tr: adj. 兼职的；部分时间的
words.ex: He works part-time at a coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家咖啡店做兼职。
words.en: If someone is a part-time worker or has a part-time job, they work for only part of each day or week.

words.ex: He will participate in the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他将参与学校的戏剧演出。
words.en: To take part in an activity or event.

words.tr: n. 伙伴关系；合作；合作关系；
words.ex: They formed a partnership to run a small shop.
words.ex_cn: 他们建立了一种伙伴关系来经营一家小店。
words.en: A partnership is a legal form of business operation between two or more individuals who share management and profits.

words.ex: He got a patent for his new invention.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的新发明获得了专利。
words.en: A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.

words.tr:
v. 支付；付出代价；
n. 工资；
words.ex: He will pay for the food tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会支付饭钱。
words.en: If you pay for something which you buy or for a service which you use, you give money to the person who is selling it or providing it.

words.ex: His take-home pay is $3,000 each month.
words.ex_cn: 他的税后工资是每月3000美元。
words.en: Take-home pay is the amount of money that a worker earns after all deductions such as taxes and insurance have been subtracted from their gross salary.

words.ex: The company updated the payroll last Friday.
words.ex_cn: 公司上星期五更新了职工工资册。
words.en: A payroll is a list of employees and the amount of money they are to be paid, or the total amount of money paid to the employees of a company.

words.tr:
n. 高峰；顶峰；
v. 达到高峰；达到最高值；
words.ex: The mountain peak is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 这座山的高峰被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or level of something; the pointed top of a mountain.

words.ex: Water can penetrate the soil slowly.
words.ex_cn: 水可以慢慢渗透进土壤。
words.en: To penetrate means to enter or pass through something, especially when this is difficult or when it is not obvious how to do it.

words.ex: The new app has high penetration in young markets.
words.ex_cn: 这款新应用在年轻市场中普及率很高。
words.en: The act or process of making a way into or through something; the ability to understand or find something out.

words.tr: n. 养老金；退休金；抚恤金；
words.ex: He receives a monthly pension after retiring.
words.ex_cn: 他退休后每月领取养老金。
words.en: A pension is a sum of money which a retired, widowed, or disabled person regularly receives from the state or from a former employer.

words.ex: He will perform the task tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会执行这个任务。
words.en: To perform means to carry out, accomplish, or fulfill an action, task, or function. It can also refer to the act of presenting a form of entertainment, such as a play, concert, or other artistic expression, before an audience.

words.ex: His performance in the game was excellent.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中的表现非常出色。
words.en: The act of performing a play, concert, or some other form of entertainment.

words.tr: phrase. 绩效评估；工作表现评价；业绩考核
words.ex: The company conducts performance appraisals every year to evaluate employees' work.
words.ex_cn: 公司每年进行绩效评估以评价员工的工作。
words.en: A performance appraisal is a systematic and periodic process that assesses an individual employee's job performance and productivity in relation to certain pre-established criteria and organizational objectives.

words.ex: Free lunch is a perk of this job.
words.ex_cn: 免费午餐是这份工作的一个额外补贴。
words.en: If someone perks up or if something perks them up, they become more cheerful or lively.

words.tr: phrase. 小额现金；小额备用金
words.ex: She used the petty cash to buy office supplies.
words.ex_cn: 她用备用现金购买了办公用品。
words.en: A small amount of cash kept on hand for minor expenses.

words.tr: phrase. 使逐步淘汰；逐渐停止
words.ex: The company will phase out old machines next year.
words.ex_cn: 公司明年将逐步淘汰旧机器。
words.en: To gradually stop using or providing something, especially over a period of time.

words.ex: I pick the red shirt for the party.
words.ex_cn: 我为派对选择红色衬衫。
words.en: To choose something from a group of things or people, or to remove something from a place using your fingers or a tool.

words.ex: The warehouse staff uses the picking list to gather items for orders.
words.ex_cn: 仓库员工使用拣货单来收集订单的物品。
words.en: A picking list is a document used in warehouses or stores that lists the items to be picked for an order.

words.tr: phrase. 饼形图；圆形分格统计图表
words.ex: The pie chart shows the percentage of students who like different fruits.
words.ex_cn: 饼状图显示了喜欢不同水果的学生的百分比。
words.en: A pie chart is a circular statistical graphic which is divided into slices to illustrate numerical proportion.

words.ex: The pilot landed the plane safely.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员安全地降落了飞机。
words.en: A pilot is a person who operates the flying controls of an aircraft. Also, to pilot something means to test or introduce a new idea, product, etc., to see if it will be successful.

words.ex: The company built a pipeline to carry oil.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司建造了一条输送石油的管道。
words.en: A pipeline is a long pipe, often underground, through which a liquid or gas is carried over a long distance.

words.ex: The plant capacity has been increased to meet the growing demand.
words.ex_cn: 工厂产能已经提高，以满足不断增长的需求。
words.en: The maximum output that a plant can produce under normal conditions.

words.tr:
n. 情节；小块用地；
v. 绘图；
words.ex: The plot of the movie was very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的情节非常精彩。
words.en: A plot is a secret plan by a group of people to do something that is illegal or wrong, especially against a person or a government. It can also refer to the main events of a play, novel, movie, or similar work, devised and presented by the writer as an interrelated sequence. Additionally, a plot can be a small piece of land that is used or intended for a specific purpose.

words.ex: The company ploughs back its profits into new equipment.
words.ex_cn: 公司把利润再投资于新设备。
words.en: To reinvest profits back into the business to fuel its growth or development.

words.tr: phrase. 销售点；零售终端；POS系统（指商店中完成商品交易、付款及收据打印的位置或系统）
words.ex: The cashier scans the item at the point of sale.
words.ex_cn: 收银员在销售点扫描商品。
words.en: The point of sale (POS) is the time and place where a retail transaction is completed. At the point of sale, the merchant calculates the amount owed by the customer, indicates that amount, may prepare an invoice for the customer, and indicates the options for the customer to make payment.

words.ex: The government changed its education policy.
words.ex_cn: 政府改变了它的教育政策。
words.en: A policy is a set of ideas or plans that is used as a basis for making decisions, especially in politics, economics, or business.

words.ex: He showed his portfolio to the art teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他向美术老师展示了他作品集。
words.en: A portfolio is a set of pictures by someone, or photographs of examples of their work, which they use when entering competitions or applying for work.

words.tr: phrase. 投资组合管理；组合证券管理
words.ex: He works in portfolio management for a bank.
words.ex_cn: 他在银行从事资产管理工作。
words.en: The professional management of various securities (stocks, bonds, etc.) and assets (such as real estate) to meet specified investment goals for the benefit of the investors.

words.tr:
n. 邮件；职位；邮寄；帖子；柱；
v. 邮寄；张贴；
words.ex: I checked the post this morning.
words.ex_cn: 我今天早上检查了邮件。
words.en: To post something means to send it through the postal system or to display it publicly, such as on a noticeboard or the internet. It can also refer to the act of assigning someone to a particular job or position.

words.tr: n. 位置；职位；地位；姿势；
words.ex: The book is on the table in a good position.
words.ex_cn: 书放在桌子上的一个好位置。
words.en: A position refers to the place or type of role someone has in a situation, organization, or society, or the way in which someone or something is placed or arranged.

words.tr:
n. 潜力；
adj. 潜在的；
words.ex: The young athlete shows great potential.
words.ex_cn: 这位年轻运动员展现出巨大的潜力。
words.en: If you say that someone or something has potential, you mean that they have the necessary abilities or qualities to become successful or useful in the future.

words.tr:
n. 力量；电源；权力；强国；
v. 给…提供能量；供以动力；
words.ex: The power of the storm broke the trees.
words.ex_cn: 风暴的力量折断了树木。
words.en: The ability or capacity to do something or act in a particular way; control or influence over others; electrical energy supplied to a device or building.

words.ex: Inflation reduces her purchasing power.
words.ex_cn: 通货膨胀降低了她的购买力。
words.en: The ability of a unit of currency to buy goods and services, often considered in relation to inflation.

words.tr: phrase. 公共关系；公关活动；公众形象管理
words.ex: He works in public relations for a big company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家大公司从事公共关系工作。
words.en: Public relations (PR) is the practice of managing the spread of information between an individual or an organization and the public.

words.ex: The company issued preference shares to raise capital.
words.ex_cn: 公司发行了优先股以筹集资金。
words.en: Preference shares are a type of share that gives the holder a fixed dividend and priority over ordinary shareholders in the event of liquidation.

words.ex: The price of bread is too high.
words.ex_cn: 面包的价格太高了。
words.en: The amount of money expected, required, or given in payment for something.

words.tr: phrase. 市场价格；市价；市场售价
words.ex: The market price of gold has increased significantly this year.
words.ex_cn: n. 今年黄金的市场价格大幅上涨。
words.en: The price at which a commodity, security, or service is selling in the marketplace.

words.ex: The retail price of this product is quite high.
words.ex_cn: 这个产品的零售价格相当高。
words.en: The price at which goods are sold to the public by retailers.

words.ex: He is on probation for one year.
words.ex_cn: 他被判缓刑一年。
words.en: Probation is a period of time during which someone who has committed a crime has to behave well and not commit any more crimes in order to avoid being sent to prison.

words.ex: This company makes a new product every year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司每年都会推出一种新产品。
words.en: A product is something that is produced and sold in large quantities, often as a result of a manufacturing process.

words.tr: phrase. 生产周期；从原材料投入到成品产出的整个生产流程
words.ex: The production cycle for this model is approximately three months.
words.ex_cn: 这个型号的生产周期大约是三个月。
words.en: The series of stages through which a product passes from its conception to its final form, including design, manufacturing, and distribution.

words.ex: The factory manager reviewed the production schedule to ensure all deadlines were met.
words.ex_cn: 工厂经理审查了生产计划，以确保所有截止日期都已满足。
words.en: A production schedule is a plan that outlines what products need to be produced, when they should be produced, and in what quantities, to meet customer demand efficiently.

words.ex: Understanding the product life cycle helps companies plan for market changes.
words.ex_cn: 理解产品生命周期有助于公司为市场变化做计划。
words.en: The stages through which a product passes from its conception to its withdrawal from the market, including introduction, growth, maturity, and decline.

words.tr: phrase. 一个企业售出的各类产品；产品组合；一种产品的不同型号
words.ex: The company is planning to expand its product mix to attract more customers.
words.ex_cn: 该公司计划扩大其产品组合以吸引更多客户。
words.en: The variety of products or services that a company offers or a market provides.

words.tr: adj. 富有成效的；多产的；生产的；
words.ex: He had a productive day and finished all his work.
words.ex_cn: 他度过了富有成效的一天，完成了所有工作。
words.en: Producing or able to produce large amounts of goods, crops, or other commodities.
